ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AC$ is the diameter of the circle $\odot O$, $P$ is the midpoint of the semicircle $AC$. Line $AP$ is extended to point $B$ such that $PB=AP$. Lines $CP$, $CB$, and $OP$ are drawn. $BC$ is a tangent of circle $\odot O$. If $AC=4$, what is the area of the shaded section in the figure?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $AC=4$,\\
thus $BC=AC=4$, $OA=OP=2$,\\
since $P$ is the midpoint of the semicircle $AC$,\\
hence $AC\perp OP$,\\
therefore $S_{\text{shaded}}=S_{\triangle ABC}-S_{\triangle AOP}-S_{\text{sector} POC}=\frac{1}{2}\times 4\times 4-\frac{1}{2}\times 2\times 2-\frac{90^\circ\pi \times 2^2}{360}=\boxed{6-\pi}$

method.method_draft: Use a local decomposition around triangle PBC. From the image, read that the shaded region is inside triangle PBC but outside the circular arc PC; thus it equals area of triangle PBC minus the circular segment cut off by chord PC. From the text, AC=4 gives radius OA=OC=OP=2. Since P is the midpoint of the semicircle, OP is perpendicular to AC and angle POC=90 degrees. Also, because BC is tangent at C, BC is perpendicular to OC, so BC is vertical in the diagram. The line AP passes through A and P; with OA=OP=2, triangle AOP is right isosceles, so AP has 45-degree direction. Extending AP by an equal length places B on the tangent through C, giving BC=4 and horizontal distance from P to BC equal to 2. Hence area triangle PBC = (1/2)(BC)(distance from P to BC)=1/2*4*2=4. The circular segment between chord PC and arc PC has area sector POC minus triangle POC = pi - 2. Therefore shaded area = 4 - (pi - 2)=6 - pi.
